3. ## ***Business Rules and Guard Rails***

This section defines system-enforced business rules that prevent scheduling conflicts on the shared DASIG Facebook Page and enforce minimum content-quality gates before publication. Rules are enforced automatically by the application, replacing what previously required manual coordination by a single Administrator. The hard- and soft-rule thresholds and the enforcement switch are adjustable by the Administrator in Settings → Page without requiring code changes, and are expected to be tuned based on operational experience during and after the pilot period. Trigger-rule thresholds are fixed in code or set by deployment configuration.

1. ### ***Guard Rail Rules*** {#guard-rail-rules}

   1. #### *Hard Rules* {#hard-rules}

Hard rules are absolute. The system rejects any action that violates them and provides an explanatory message with suggested alternatives. 

| Rule ID | Rule Name | Threshold | Enforcement Point | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| GR-H1 | **Conflict Buffer** | No two posts within ±30 minutes on the shared DASIG Facebook Page  | At slot selection (UC-1.8); re-validated at submission (UC-1.9); at Moderator and Administrator rescheduling (UC-3.1); enforced in the database by an exclusion constraint (UC-3.1 A4) | Prevents audience saturation and Facebook algorithm penalties on the shared single page  |
| GR-H2 | **Minimum Lead Time** | Scheduled time must be ≥2 hours in the future  | At slot selection; re-validated at submission (UC-1.9)  | Ensures the Administrator has sufficient time to review content before publication. Does not apply to Live Event Fast-Track submissions (UC-1.5), which have no scheduled time.  |
| GR-H3 | **Maximum Lead Time** | Scheduled time must be ≤30 days in the future  | At slot selection; re-validated at submission  | Prevents calendar chaos and stale content  |
| GR-H4 | **Posting Window** | Scheduled time must fall between 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM (Asia/Manila) | At slot selection (UC-1.8); re-validated at submission (UC-1.9); at rescheduling (UC-3.1) | Publishes when the Page audience is active |
| GR-H5 | **Approval-Before-Publish Gate**  | A submission cannot be published until an Administrator has approved it (state must be `SCHEDULED`, not `PENDING_APPROVAL` or `IN_REVIEW`)  | At publishing scheduler query (UC-3.2)   | Guarantees a quality control step before public posting. (Numbered GR-H4 in SRS v6.0; renumbered so that GR-H4 matches the rule code the system reports for the posting window.) |

**Configurable threshold table — Hard Rules:**

| Rule ID | Configurable | Default  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| GR-H1 | Yes — conflict buffer duration (default: 30 min) Settings → Page  | 30 minutes  |
| GR-H2 | Yes — minimum lead time (default: 2 hours) Settings → Page | 2 hours |
| GR-H3 | Yes — maximum lead time (default: 30 days) Settings → Page | 30 days |
| GR-H4 | Yes — window start and end hour, Settings → Page | 8:00 AM–8:00 PM |
| GR-H5 | No — structural rule, not a threshold | \-  |

#### 

Enforcement of GR-H1–GR-H4 can be switched off network-wide in Settings → Page; a Standard post still needs a future time and a slot reservation. The database exclusion constraint behind GR-H1 uses a fixed ±30-minute range, so the buffer should stay at 30 minutes unless that constraint is migrated.

2. #### *Soft Rules* {#soft-rules}

Soft rules generate warnings but allow the action to proceed without blocking. Contributors and Administrators may proceed through a soft rule warning without explicit confirmation. Hard rule violations block the action entirely for Contributors; an Administrator may override a hard rule during their own actions (e.g., drag-rescheduling, UC-3.1 A2) with a mandatory written justification, but there is no Contributor-initiated override request mechanism in this version of the system. 

| Rule ID | Rule Name | Threshold | Enforcement Point | Rationale |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| GR-S1 | Per-Institution Active Quota | Each institution may have at most 3 scheduled-but-unpublished posts at any time. Does not apply to Live Event Fast-Track submissions, which do not enter a scheduled-but-unpublished state. | At slot selection (UC-1.8); re-checked at submission (UC-1.9)  | Prevents one institution from monopolizing the calendar; ensures fairness across DASIG member institutions  |
| GR-S2 | Daily Volume Cap | The DASIG Facebook Page may have at most 6 scheduled posts per calendar day across all institutions, inclusive of Live Event Fast-Track publications counted on their actual publish date. | At slot selection (UC-1.8); at approval for Fast-Track submissions (UC-2.4 A8)  | Prevents audience fatigue from burst posting on the shared page  |

**Configurable threshold table — Soft Rules:**

| Rule ID | Configurable | Default |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| GR-S1 | Yes — per-institution active post quota, Settings → Page | 3 posts |
| GR-S2 | Yes — daily volume cap, Settings → Page | 6 posts |

#### 

3. #### *Trigger Rules* {#trigger-rules}

Trigger rules cause the system to act autonomously — dispatching notifications, escalating priority, transitioning states, or performing cleanup — without human request. 

| Rule ID | Rule Name | Trigger Condition | System Action |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| GR-T1  | Approaching Publish Time Priority Flag  | submission.state IN ('PENDING\_APPROVAL', 'IN\_REVIEW') AND scheduled\_at \< NOW() \+ 30 minutes  | Show a priority badge ("Priority \<30m") on the submission in the Review Queue (UC-2.4), computed each time the queue is read. The non-paginated queue endpoint also sorts these items first; the paginated queue used by the Review Queue screen orders Fast-Track first and then by the chosen sort, so there the item is flagged but not moved. No escalation notification is sent at this stage. If the submission remains unreviewed past its scheduled time, it transitions to MISSED\_REVIEW per GR-T9 and is listed in the Approval Queue's Failed tab (UC-2.4 A8) |
| GR-T2  | Slot Reservation Cleanup  | `DRAFT` submission with held slot reservation; no activity for 7 days  | Automatically release the slot reservation. The `DRAFT` record is retained in the Contributor's Submission Queue. No notification is sent.  |
| GR-T3 | Token Expiry Warning | facebook\_token.expires\_at \< NOW() \+ 7 days | Send Administrator in-app \+ email notification (T-08).  |
| GR-T4 | Token Validation Failure  | Daily token health check API call fails or returns an invalid response  | Record the failed check (the token row is not deactivated). Send Administrator in-app and email alert (T-09). Suspend automated publishing for all `SCHEDULED` submissions until the token is reauthorized (UC-3.5 A5).  |
| GR-T5 | Publishing Retry Sequence | Publishing API call (UC-3.2) fails  | Retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff (5s, 25s, 125s). If all retries fail, transition submission to `PUBLISH_FAILED` and alert Administrator (T-06).  |
| GR-T6 | High-Volume Failure Consolidation | More than 5 PUBLISH\_FAILED events within a rolling hour | Failures 1–5 alert Administrators individually; the 6th sends one consolidated high-priority alert (T-06; in-app, email, and Messenger per UC-3.3 A4) linking to the Failed tab; later failures in the same rolling hour send no individual Administrator alerts. Individual PUBLISH\_FAILED records are still created and visible in the Approval Queue's Failed tab (UC-2.4 A8), and Contributors are still notified. |
| GR-T7 | Media AI Processing and Embedding Reconciliation | An image asset is uploaded, or an image asset lacks a current embedding | **Scope:** Image assets only. Video assets are permanently excluded from the classification and embedding pipeline supporting the media library, drafting, and album-matching features (UC-2.1, UC-1.7, UC-2.2) and will always have embedding \= NULL by design. The asset type filter prevents the job from repeatedly attempting to embed video assets. Processing: each upload queues a classify-and-embed job in the durable media\_processing\_jobs queue; a worker polls every second, claims jobs under a lease, calls Google Gemini for classification and then Voyage AI for the image and semantic embeddings, and marks the asset READY. On success: the vectors are stored in media\_asset\_embeddings and the asset becomes immediately available for semantic similarity search, including AI-Suggested Media during drafting (UC-1.7). On failure: the job is retried with backoff up to 5 attempts and then moved to a dead letter, and the asset is marked FAILED; an Administrator can list and retry dead letters (UC-3.5 A6). Reconciliation: the EmbeddingReconciliationJob (default every 30 seconds) re-queues images still missing current embeddings, in bounded batches. The Administrator receives a weekly digest notification (T-12, in-app) of assets whose embedding failed. No user-facing error is shown to Contributors. |
| GR-T8 | Invitation Token Expiry Detection | account.state IN ('PENDING', 'PENDING\_EMAIL\_UNDELIVERED') AND account.invitation\_token\_expires\_at \< NOW()  | Transition account to `EXPIRED` state. Retain account record. Surface in the account management panel with reason: "Invitation token expired without activation." No user-facing notification is sent. The Administrator may reissue a new token at any time (`EXPIRED` → `PENDING`, per the Account State Machine). Schedule: hourly. |
| GR-T9 | Stale Submission Detection | submission.state IN ('SCHEDULED', 'PENDING\_APPROVAL', 'IN\_REVIEW') AND submission.scheduled\_at \< NOW() − INTERVAL '5 minutes'; or a Fast-Track submission stuck in a publishing state for more than 5 minutes  | If state \= 'SCHEDULED': transition to PUBLISH\_FAILED, reason "missed\_publish\_window — server dormancy or cron failure." If state IN ('PENDING\_APPROVAL', 'IN\_REVIEW') and no review lock is held: transition to MISSED\_REVIEW, reason "scheduled time passed without review," and release the slot. A stuck Fast-Track publish transitions to PUBLISH\_FAILED. Notify Administrators in each case. The submission is listed in the Approval Queue's Failed tab (UC-2.4 A8); a MISSED\_REVIEW item returns to PENDING\_APPROVAL once a new slot is chosen. Schedule: every 5 minutes. |

Configurable threshold table — Trigger Rules:

| Rule ID | Configurable | Default |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| GR-T1 | No — fixed in code | 30 minutes (linked with GR-H2) |
| GR-T2 | No — fixed in code | 7 days |
| GR-T3 | No — fixed in code | 7 days |
| GR-T4 | No — structural check, fires on failure | — |
| GR-T5 | No — fixed in code | 3 attempts; 5s, 25s, 125s |
| GR-T6 | No — fixed in code | 5 failures per hour |
| GR-T7 | Deployment configuration — worker batch, lease, attempts, poll and reconcile intervals | 5 attempts; reconcile every 30 s |
| GR-T8 | No — fires when token expiry timestamp is crossed | — |
| GR-T9 | No — fixed in code | 5 minutes |

#### 

4. #### *Override & Administrative Action Audit Requirements*  {#override-&-administrative-action-audit-requirements}

All hard rule overrides by an Administrator (e.g., drag-rescheduling into a conflict, UC-3.1 A2) and all Edit & Approve actions performed by a Moderator or Administrator that modify submitted content before publication (UC-2.4 A9–A10) are recorded in the immutable audit log with the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| ----- | ----- |
| Actor | User ID and name of the person (Administrator or Moderator) performing the action |
| Action type | Reschedule Override, Edit & Approve, or other logged action category |
| Rule(s) affected (if applicable) | Rule ID and name for any hard rule overridden (e.g., GR-H1), with threshold value at time of action |
| Before/after values | For Edit: the diff of changed fields. For reschedule overrides: original and new scheduled time |
| Written justification | Mandatory reason text entered by the Administrator. (Note: Required only for hard rule overrides; not required for standard Edit actions) |
| Timestamp | ISO 8601 |
| Affected submission ID | The unique ID of the specific submission/post that was edited or rescheduled. |

> **Audit Log Surfacing:** All entries are accessible via **System & Audit → Audit Log** (UC-3.6), viewable and filterable by the Administrator or Super Administrator, with export available for DASIG/DOST Region 7 governance reporting. 

2. ### ***Application Business Rules*** {#application-business-rules}

This section consolidates operational rules extracted from the use case descriptions, collected here so that threshold values, constraints, and behavioral specifications have a single authoritative location in the SRS. 

#### 

1. #### *User Provisioning and Account Management*  {#user-provisioning-and-account-management}

   **BR-ACC-01 — Contributor Provisioning Status Restriction.** Contributor invitation (UC-1.3) is restricted to institutions in `ACTIVE` status only. Contributors may not be added to an institution that is inactive or pending setup. 

   **BR-ACC-02 — Password Complexity Requirements.** Passwords must satisfy all of the following simultaneously: minimum 12 characters; at least one uppercase letter; at least one lowercase letter; at least one digit; at least one special character; must contain no spaces; must not be a common or sequential password (enforced by the zxcvbn strength meter); must not include the user's name or email Enforced in real time with inline validation feedback per rule; the Submit button remains disabled until all requirements are met. Applies at account activation (UC-1.1/UC-1.3) and both password paths (UC-1.4 A5, A6). 

   **BR-ACC-03 — Institutional Email Domain Matching.** When sending an invitation to a Contributor and the assigned institution has a registered email domain, the recipient's email address domain must strictly match that domain (e.g., @university.edu). Mismatches are rejected by the system.

   **BR-ACC-04 — Invitation Token Validity.** Invitation Tokens expire 72 hours after generation, are single-use, and are scoped to the recipient's institution (for Contributors) or network-wide (for Administrators). A token generated for one institution's Contributor cannot activate an account at a different institution; mismatch returns a generic invalid-token error. When a token is reissued, the previous token is explicitly invalidated before the new one is generated. 

   **BR-ACC-05 — Password Reset Token Validity.** Password Reset Tokens expire 1 hour after generation and are single-use. Any previously issued, unused reset token for the same account is invalidated when a new one is generated. 

   **BR-ACC-06 — Post-Login Landing Route.** On successful login, every role lands on /dashboard; the dashboard content and navigation are role-specific (UC-1.4 step 5).

   **BR-ACC-07 — Post-Login Feature Access by Role.** On first login following account activation, the system grants the following role-specific access:

| Feature | Contributor | Moderator | Administrator  |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Content submission form (Propose New Post) | ✓ (own institution)  | ✓ (Posting As any institution)  | ✓ (Posting As any institution)  |
| Master Calendar | Read-only, network-wide timing | Full detail; reschedule within caps | Full edit access, with override |
| Media Library | Own institution \+ shared library | Network-wide | Network-wide; Trash |
| Analytics Dashboard | Institution-scoped, read-only | Network-wide (no institution filter) | Network-wide, with institution filter and Administrator-only reports |
| Validation Queue | — | Full access | Full access |
| Institution Management | — | Read-only  | Full access |
| Invitations | — | Contributors only | All roles |
| System Health, Audit Log, Page and Watermark Settings, Admin and User Management | — | — | Full access |

   **BR-ACC-08 — Administrator Headcount Cap.** To enforce security and limit broad network access, the system restricts the number of Administrators — active Administrators plus outstanding Administrator invitations plus pending promotions — to a combined cap (default: 3, app.admins.max). If the network is at capacity, new Administrator invitations are blocked until an existing Admin is demoted or deactivated.

   **BR-ACC-09 — Deactivated Account Reactivation.** An account that has been explicitly deactivated cannot be "re-invited" through the standard invitation flow to bypass their deactivated status. The system will throw a conflict error; they must be manually reactivated by an Administrator.

   **BR-ACC-10 — Invitation Role Hierarchy.** Administrators can invite any role (Contributor, Moderator, or Admin). Moderators are network-wide and can invite Contributors to any institution, but they are forbidden from generating invitations for other Moderators or Administrators.

   2. #### *Content Submission*   {#content-submission}

   **BR-SUB-01 — Accepted File Types and Upload Size Limit.** Accepted image formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF. Accepted video formats: MP4, MOV, WebM. Each file's declared MIME type, extension, and size are validated on the client and the server before storage; file-content (magic-byte) inspection is not performed. Maximum file size: 50 MB per file. 

   **BR-SUB-02 — Media Asset Limit per Submission.** A submission may include a combined maximum of 10 media assets (device-uploaded, repository-linked, or AI-suggested). Enforced at the point of adding each asset, across all attachment methods (UC-1.7). 

   **BR-SUB-03 — Draft Slot Reservation Timeout.** A tentatively reserved slot held by a DRAFT submission is automatically released after a configured period of inactivity (default: 7 consecutive days) per the GR-T2 trigger rule. The `DRAFT` record is retained with no active slot; the Contributor must reselect a slot on next open. Does not apply to Live Event Fast-Track drafts, which hold no slot. 

   **BR-SUB-04 — AI Processing Windows.** AI classification tags and caption suggestions are expected within 10 seconds of upload or request. Media recommendations (AI-Suggested Media, UC-1.7) appear within 3 seconds of event-detail input. Target windows only; if AI services are unavailable, the system degrades silently (UC-1.6 A2). 

   **BR-SUB-05 — Mixed Media Publishing Restriction**. A single submission containing both images and videos cannot be automatically published via the Facebook Graph API. The system automatically flags any mixed-media post with requiresManualPublishing \= true, requiring the Administrator to manually publish the content on Facebook and reconcile the status.

   **BR-SUB-06 — Caption Length Limit.** The post caption must not exceed 3,000 characters (code-point count). Enforced both in the frontend composer UI and the backend validation service. 

      3. #### *Media and Asset Management*    {#media-and-asset-management}

   **BR-MED-01 — Network View Access.** The Media Library allows Administrators and Moderators to view assets across all institutions. This Network View is the default scope for network-level roles, though they may explicitly filter the view down to individual institutions using the provided UI filters.

   **BR-MED-02 — Asset Deletion Precedence.** Before deleting an asset: if referenced in a `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `IN_REVIEW`, or `SCHEDULED` submission, deletion is blocked. If referenced only in `DRAFT` or `NEEDS_REVISION` submissions, deletion is allowed with a confirmation prompt warning the reference will break. If referenced only in terminal-state submissions (`REJECTED`, `PUBLISHED`, `PUBLISHED_MANUAL`, `PUBLISH_FAILED`) or unreferenced, deletion is allowed with a simple confirmation. Deletion is a soft delete: the asset moves to the Trash, where an Administrator may restore or permanently delete it; items still in the Trash after 30 days are purged together with their stored file (UC-2.3 A5). 

         4. #### *Content Approval*    {#content-approval}

   **BR-APP-01 — Review Lock Timeout.** If the Administrator or Moderator holding a review lock takes no action for 15 consecutive minutes, the lock expires and the submission automatically reverts from IN\_REVIEW to PENDING\_APPROVAL, becoming available for another reviewer (UC-2.4 A4). 

   **BR-APP-02 — Revision Remarks Requirements.** Revision remarks are mandatory when requesting a revision. Minimum length: 10 characters. Maximum length: 1,000 characters. The Request Revision action is blocked until the minimum is met, and the field rejects input beyond the maximum.

   **BR-APP-03 — Rejection Reason Codes.** When rejecting a submission, the reviewer must select from the following standardized reason codes. Written notes are optional for all codes except OTHER. Missing or fixable content (e.g., wrong format, incomplete details) must be routed through Request Revision rather than rejected. A rejected submission is not final: the Contributor may edit and resubmit it.

| Code | Label |
| ----- | ----- |
| INAPPROPRIATE\_CONTENT | Content violates DASIG posting guidelines. |
| OUT\_OF\_SCOPE | Not a DASIG activity or related to the network. |
| DUPLICATE\_EVENT | This event has already been submitted or published |
| NO\_LONGER\_RELEVANT | Event has passed and is no longer timely. |
| RIGHTS\_OR\_PRIVACY | Rights, copyright, or privacy issue. |
| WRONG\_INSTITUTION | Content belongs to another institution. |
| OTHER | Other |

   #### **BR-APP-04 — Self-Review Restriction**. An Administrator or Moderator may not review, approve, request revisions for, or reject their own submissions. The system unconditionally blocks self-review; another privileged user must perform the validation.  {#br-app-04-—-self-review-restriction.-an-administrator-or-moderator-may-not-review,-approve,-request-revisions-for,-or-reject-their-own-submissions.-the-system-unconditionally-blocks-self-review;-another-privileged-user-must-perform-the-validation.}

   **BR-APP-05 — Fast-Track Override Restriction.** Toggling the "Live Event Fast-Track" status of a submission during an active review session is restricted to Administrators. Regular Moderators may edit other submission details but cannot bypass the queue by converting a standard submission to Fast-Track (or vice versa).

         5. #### *Notification Behavior*      {#notification-behavior}

   **BR-NOT-01 — Notification Delivery Timing.** In-app: Real-time via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Email: within 5 minutes in ≥95% of cases. Facebook Messenger: best-effort, subject to Meta's Messenger Platform delivery. All notifications include a direct deep-link to the affected submission, queue tab, or relevant view — never a generic dashboard link.

   **BR-NOT-02 — Notification Bell and Read-State.** The notification bell badge increments by one for each unread in-app notification and persists across page refreshes and sessions (read-state is server-persisted). A notification is marked as read when the user clicks the item or uses Mark All Read. Opening the notification panel alone does not mark notifications as read. The badge count decrements only as individual notifications are clicked or all are bulk-marked.

   **BR-NOT-03 — Notification Panel Behavior.** The panel displays the 50 most recent notifications per user, newest first. View All Notifications opens a paginated full-history view. Notifications are retained indefinitely in the database; there is no automatic 90-day archive or purge (except upon account deletion).

   **BR-NOT-04 — Notification Preferences.**Users may independently toggle their preferences for In-App and Email notifications via their account settings. Facebook Messenger delivery is strictly opt-in and restricted by role: only Administrators and Moderators may connect their accounts to Messenger; Contributors are blocked from this channel.

   **BR-NOT-05 — Cross-Session Synchronization.** Notification read-state actions (read single, mark all read) instantly broadcast an SSE sync event to all active sessions for that user, ensuring the notification bell badge decrements simultaneously across all open browser tabs.

         6. #### *Analytics*      {#analytics}

   **BR-ANA-01 — KPI Definitions and Formulas.**

* **AVG POSTING DELAY** — AVG(published\_at − first\_pending\_at) where state IN (PUBLISHED, PUBLISHED\_MANUAL) within the selected period. first\_pending\_at is the first transition to PENDING\_APPROVAL. Display: Days (calculated as epoch seconds ÷ 86400). Target: ≤1.0 days.  
* **CONTENT COMPLETENESS** — COUNT(posts meeting all required criteria) ÷ COUNT(all published posts) × 100%. Required fields: non-empty event title, non-null event date, non-empty caption, at least one valid media asset. Target: ≥95%.  
* **TOTAL POSTS PUBLISHED** — COUNT(PUBLISHED) \+ COUNT(PUBLISHED\_MANUAL) within the selected period. Target: ≥4 posts per institution per month. 

		**BR-ANA-02 — Period-over-Period Delta Comparison Periods.**

| Selected Range | Comparison Period |
| ----- | ----- |
| 7d | Previous 7 days |
| 30d | Previous 30 days |
| 90d | Previous 90 days |
| YTD | Jan 1 to same date, prior calendar year |

If no data exists for the comparison period, the delta displays "N/A." 

**BR-ANA-03 — Sparkline Behavior.** Each KPI tile shows a 12-week sparkline. For deployments with fewer than 12 weeks of data, weeks prior to deployment evaluate to zero (0) in the backend.

**BR-ANA-04 — AI Performance Metrics Scope by Role.** The AI-performance report and export are restricted to Administrators (other roles receive 403 Forbidden). AI feature adoption — caption suggestions, media suggestions, album Auto-Match, top-post templates, and the writing check — is shown to Administrators on the Analytics dashboard, network-wide and filterable by institution.

Minimum threshold for display: 20 total AI events (across all AI features combined) within the selected period/scope; otherwise dimmed with an insufficient-data notice.

**BR-ANA-05 — Operational Health Metrics.** These metrics are restricted to Administrators only.

Contributors and Moderators do not have access.

| Metric | Contributor | Administrator |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AI caption acceptance rate | Own submissions only | Network-wide (filterable) |
| AI tag manual-correction rate | Own submissions only | Network-wide (filterable) |

* Minimum threshold for display: 20 total AI events (across all AI features combined) within the selected period/scope; otherwise dimmed with an insufficient-data notice.

  **BR-ANA-05 — Operational Health Metrics.** These metrics are restricted to Administrators only. Contributors and Moderators do not have access. 

| Metric | Definition |
| ----- | ----- |
| Submissions Entered Workflow | Count of submissions that entered the pending state |
| Validation Deadline Risks | Count and percentage of submissions approaching the review |
| Override Audit Events | Count and percentage of administrative override actions taken  |
| Missed review rate | Count of submissions transitioned to `MISSED_REVIEW` (GR-T9) per week |
| Publication Attempts | Total system attempts to publish to social channels |
| Successful Publications | Total successful publications and overall success rate |
| On-time Publication | Count and percentage of scheduled posts published on time (Target: ≥95%) |

		The missed-review rate (share of review outcomes in the last 30 days that were MISSED\_REVIEW, 		flagged above 10%) is shown on System Health (UC-3.5), not on the Analytics dashboard.

**BR-ANA-06 — Full Report Submission-Level Table Column Visibility.**

| Column | Contributor | Moderator | Administrator |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Submission ID | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Event title | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Contributor name | — | ✓ | ✓ |
| Institution | — | — | ✓ |
| First submitted date | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published date | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Publication state | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Posting delay (hours) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Completeness | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Revision cycles count | — | ✓ | ✓ |

Exported CSV files are named: DASIGConnect\_Analytics\_\[Role\]\_\[Institution or Network\]\_\[DateRange\].csv. 

7. #### *Publishing*      {#publishing}

   **BR-PUB-01 — Calendar Card State Specification.**

| Submission State | Card Label | Visual Indicator |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| DRAFT  | "\[Institution\] — Draft"  | Grey, solid border  |
| PENDING\_APPROVAL | "\[Institution\] — Pending Approval" | Light grey, dashed border |
| NEEDS\_REVISION | "\[Institution\] — Needs Revision" | Amber, dashed border  |
| SCHEDULED | "\[Institution\] — \[Title\]" | Institution color, solid border |
| PUBLISHING | "\[Institution\] — Publishing..." | Institution color, solid border with spinner |
| PUBLISHED | "\[Institution\] — \[Title\]" | Green, solid border |
| PUBLISHED\_MANUAL | "\[Institution\] — \[Title\] (Manual)" | Teal, solid border |
| PUBLISH\_FAILED | "\[Institution\] — \[Title\] (Failed)" | Red, solid border |
| MISSED\_REVIEW | "\[Institution\] — \[Title\] (Missed review)" | Distinct missed-review color |

   Live Event Fast-Track submissions do not appear with a reserved slot (UC-3.1 A4); if shown, they appear as an unscheduled marker on their publish date. Each card shows the institution badge, title (truncated to 40 characters), and scheduled time.

   **BR-PUB-02 — Publishing Scheduler Windows.** The primary publishing scheduler runs every minute and picks up SCHEDULED submissions whose scheduled time falls within a 5-minute lookback window, accounting for brief server lag or cron delay. To prevent duplicate posts across instances, submissions are atomically claimed and transitioned to a transient publishing state before any platform API calls are made. Transient API failures log to publication\_attempts and are retried within this window.The secondary stale-submission scheduler (GR-T9) runs every 5 minutes and detects submissions missed beyond the 5-minute window, transitioning scheduled ones to PUBLISH\_FAILED and unreviewed ones to MISSED\_REVIEW.

   **BR-PUB-03 — Automated Publishing Asset Type Support.**

| Asset Type | Publishing Path |
| ----- | ----- |
| Image-only (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF) | Multi-photo two-step method: stage each image individually, then publish a single feed post with all photo IDs attached |
| Video-only (MP4, MOV, WebM) | Single-call video publish method via /{PAGE\_ID}/videos |
| Mixed (images \+ video in same submission) | Mixed-media submissions transition to `PUBLISH_FAILED`; recovery via the Approval Queue's Failed tab (UC-2.4 A8).  |

   **BR-PUB-04 — Manual Publishing Audit Log Fields.** The audit log entry on PUBLISHED\_MANUAL transition includes: Administrator identity, submission ID, original scheduled time (if any), PUBLISHED\_MANUAL timestamp, validated platform post URL, written notes, and prior state (PUBLISH\_FAILED).

   **BR-PUB-05 — Manual Publishing Analytics Impact.** PUBLISHED\_MANUAL submissions are included in all three primary KPIs (BR-ANA-01): counted in TOTAL POSTS PUBLISHED, included in AVG POSTING DELAY, and evaluated in CONTENT COMPLETENESS. 

   **BR-PUB-06 — Manual Publishing Workflow & Abandonment.** The manual publishing fallback requires a valid live platform URL to be provided before the submission can be marked as `PUBLISHED_MANUAL`. The workflow enforces a 2-hour countdown window. If the Administrator cancels the flow, a `MANUAL_PUBLISH_CANCELLED` audit log is written. If the 2-hour window expires without completion, the system automatically clears the lock, sets `lastManualPublishAbandonedAt`, and writes a `MANUAL_PUBLISH_ABANDONED` event to the audit log.

   8. #### *AI Features*     {#ai-features}

   **BR-AI-01 — Caption Generation Prompt Parameters.**

| Parameter | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Language | English |
| Role instruction | Social media content writer for a Philippine government-affiliated academic network (DOST DASIG) |
| Task | Generate one Facebook caption variants for the provided image(s) and event context. Apply intent detection on any existing text in the caption field: determine if it is a direct instruction to follow, or a draft caption to refine. |
| Tone variants | One of Professional (default), Community, or Energetic, chosen by the user. If user text is detected as an instruction, the caption follows that guidance within the chosen tone. |
| Output format | A single caption for the selected tone |
| Security | Enforces prompt injection defense on user-supplied text. The output-token limit is sized from the requested length. |
| Safety constraints | No profanity, hate speech, discriminatory language, political opinions, unsupported factual claims, or unrelated commercial endorsements; appropriate for a government-affiliated academic audience |
| Context inputs | Up to 4 base64-encoded images (resized \<5MB), event title, event date, institution, media metadata and AI tags, existing caption text, and an optional instruction of up to 280 characters. |

   **BR-AI-02 — Caption Suggestion Re-generate Debounce.** Re-generate requests are debounced at 3 seconds. Repeated clicks within 3 seconds of a prior call trigger only one request. A loading indicator is shown during the debounce and API call period. 

   **BR-AI-03 — Caption Interaction Logging Schema.** Each caption suggestion interaction is logged with: whether a suggestion was shown, action taken (use / use\_then\_edited / edit / re-generate / dismiss), tone selected if applicable, submission ID, and timestamp. If the user applies the caption and subsequently modifies the caption field before submitting, the logged action is updated from use to use\_then\_edited to distinguish clean acceptance from accepted-but-revised for KPI accuracy. 

   **BR-AI-04 — Image Classification Prompt Parameters (Google Gemini).**

| Parameter | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Task | Classify the image into exactly one of 14 predefined categories and one asset type, provide a factual description, and generate up to 30 tags plus enrichment signals (observed scenes, possible use cases, temporal classification).. |
| Category taxonomy | Food, People, Event, Technology, Research, Education, Sports, Culture, Nature, Document, Product, Architecture, Artwork, Other |
| Output format | JSON only — no prose or markdown (primary\_category, asset\_type, confidence, ai\_caption, ai\_tags, and enrichment fields) |
| Fallback rule | Always return the closest matching category even at low confidence; any value outside the taxonomy is stored as Other. |
| Provenance  | Classification timestamp, model name, and tag source (`AI` vs `MANUAL`) are persisted to the database.  |
| Safety constraint | Descriptions must not include personal information beyond visible roles or institutional contexts. |

   **BR-AI-05 — Media Recommendation Similarity Parameters.**

| Parameter | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Similarity metric | Cosine similarity via pgvector cosine distance operator |
| Vector model  | voyage-multimodal-3.5 (image) and voyage-4-lite (text), 1024 output dimensions |
| Relevance threshold | Hybrid score (semantic, visual, recency, tag, and category signals) ≥ 0.40 |
| Search context  | Event title, draft caption, media tags, and already-selected images |
| Fallback mechanism  | If the vector query fails, fall back to keyword (tag and filename) matching. |
| Search scope | The submission's institution plus the shared DASIG Central Visayas library |
| Result count | Top 8 assets above threshold, ordered by descending score |
| Title input debounce | 500ms inactivity after each keystroke |
| Panel refresh trigger | Combined event context reaches at least 10 characters, or an image is selected |

   **BR-AI-06 — Recommendation Interaction Logging Schema.** Each recommendation panel interaction is logged with: event type (recommendation\_shown / asset\_previewed / asset\_added / asset\_ignored), asset ID if applicable, similarity score, event title text at time of query, submission ID, and timestamp.

   **BR-AI-07 — AI Rate Limits.** Per user, per rolling hour: caption generation 30 requests, writing check 30 requests, template from top posts 10 requests. Exceeding a limit returns 429 Too Many Requests with the reset time.

   4. ## ***Non-functional requirements***

      1. ### ***Performance***

* Content submission form response time shall not exceed 3 seconds under normal operating load (up to 20 concurrent users).

* Master Calendar load time shall not exceed 2 seconds for displaying a 30-day window with up to 200 scheduled events.

* Guard rail validation (conflict check, quota check, lead time check) shall complete within 500 milliseconds at slot selection time, providing real-time feedback to the Contributor.

* Media asset search shall return results in ≤2 seconds for a media library of up to 1,000 assets.

* AI caption generation shall complete and display one caption within 10 seconds in ≥90% of cases. The system enforces a 30-second hard timeout to prevent hanging UI threads in the event of upstream API degradation.

* AI image classification and vector embedding shall execute asynchronously upon image upload to avoid blocking the submission response time. The asynchronous pipeline shall complete within 10 seconds of upload in ≥90% of cases.

* Media recommendation results (AI-Suggested Media, UC-1.7) shall be returned within 3 seconds of qualifying event-detail input (debounced at 500ms). This SLA is achieved by querying pre-computed pgvector embeddings rather than scanning images at request time.

* Automated post publishing shall occur within ±5 minutes of the scheduled time in ≥95% of scheduled publications, subject to the backend remaining available as described in Section 2.3 (Deployment Platform and Background Processing). During any period where the backend is unavailable, missed publish windows shall surface as PUBLISH\_FAILED items and are resolved via the Approval Queue's Failed tab (UC-2.4 A8). Missed publications due to documented server dormancy do not count against the ±5 minute SLA for pilot evaluation purposes, provided they are resolved within 30 minutes of the missed window.

* In-app notification badges and lists shall update in near real-time (≤ 1 second) of a triggering event, utilizing persistent Server-Sent Events (SSE).

* Email notifications shall be dispatched within 5 minutes of a triggering event in ≥95% of cases.

* The analytics dashboard shall reflect updated metrics within 60 seconds of a relevant system event (submission, approval, publication).

* The Approaching Publish Time Priority Flag (GR-T1) shall be computed each time the Review Queue is read, so it appears on the first queue load after the 30-minute threshold is crossed.

  2. ### ***Security***

* All client-server communication shall be encrypted via HTTPS using TLS 1.2 or higher. Unencrypted HTTP connections shall be rejected.  
* User authentication shall use a secure token-based mechanism (JWT). Tokens shall expire a fixed 8 hours after issue; API activity does not extend them. Tokens shall be invalidated upon explicit logout, and a password reset invalidates every token for the account (session\_version). A refresh endpoint (POST /api/v1/auth/refresh) exists for re-issuing a token to an authenticated user, but the frontend does not call it and it is not rate-limited; the session-expiry experience is the warning banner and re-login modal. Session expiry handling (warning banner before expiry, re-authentication prompt, draft recovery) is defined in UC-1.4 A7 and applies to all authenticated users across all roles.  
* Invitation Tokens shall be generated as cryptographically random 32-byte values, encoded as a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal string (or equivalent URL-safe encoding). Only a SHA-256 hash of the token shall be stored in the database. Generating a new invitation or resending an invite shall automatically invalidate any existing, unused tokens for that target email. Contributor tokens shall be scoped to the target institution and shall not be usable to activate accounts at a different institution.  
* Passwords shall be hashed using bcrypt or an equivalent industry-standard adaptive hashing algorithm with cost factor ≥12. Plaintext passwords shall never be stored. (Implementation note: the current build uses bcrypt with the library default cost factor of 10; raising it to 12 is an open item.)  
* All API endpoints shall enforce role-based access control. Requests that do not match the required role for an endpoint shall return a 403 Forbidden response.  
* Tenant scope (institution data isolation) shall be enforced at the database level via row-level security policies and at the application interceptor level. No user shall be able to access submissions, media assets, or workspace data belonging to a different institution.  
* The Facebook Page Access Token shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM as specified in Section 3.1.2. The encryption key shall be securely derived via a SHA-256 hash of the application's Facebook App Secret. This secret shall be stored as an environment variable and shall never be committed to version control, included in the repository, or exposed in any API response, log output, or error message.  
* File uploads utilize a direct-to-bucket presigned URL architecture. The application backend shall strictly validate the client-provided upload metadata (declared MIME type, SHA-256 content hash, and max 50 MB file size). The MIME restriction (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, MOV, WebM) is enforced on the declared type by the client and the backend. Content-level (magic-byte) inspection is not performed by the backend or the bucket in the current build.  
* Rate limiting shall be applied as follows:  
  * Login: protected by account lockout (below). Per-IP login rate limiting is not implemented and is deferred to the hosting or gateway layer.  
  * AI endpoints (on-demand only): per user per rolling hour — caption generation and re-generate 30, writing check 30, template from top posts 10 (BR-AI-07). This protects against API cost abuse. When the limit is reached, "Suggest Caption" and "Re-generate" are disabled with a message indicating the time until reset. Automatic AI calls triggered by system events — image classification on upload and media recommendation queries on event-detail input (UC-1.7) — are not subject to the per-user rate limit and are governed by the API provider's own limits. If automatic classification calls approach provider-level limits, the GR-T7 reconciliation job provides recovery for assets that fail embedding generation.  
  * Client-side debounce for AI buttons: "Suggest Caption" and "Re-generate" shall implement a 3-second client-side debounce; repeated clicks within 3 seconds trigger only one request, with a loading indicator shown throughout.  
  * Upload and all other endpoints: no per-user request rate limit is implemented in this version; such limits are deferred to the hosting or gateway layer.  
* Account lockout shall be enforced at the application level by User ID (Account-based) after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within 15 minutes; lockout duration is 15 minutes. The failed-attempt counter resets after the lockout period expires or upon a successful login. The login response is 401 Unauthorized with a lockout message showing the remaining duration; no lockout email is sent. (Note: IP-based rate limiting is deferred to the infrastructure/gateway layer).  
* All state-changing workflow and governance actions (submissions, approvals, rejections, edits, publications, reschedule overrides, account and institution changes) shall be recorded in an immutable audit log including actor ID, action, timestamp, IP address, and resource identifier. Page Settings changes, including guard-rail threshold changes, are not yet audited (see 3.4.5).  
* Hard rule overrides during Administrator rescheduling (UC-3.1 A2) shall require explicit written justification; Edit & Approve actions (UC-2.4 A9–A10) record a before/after diff without a justification. Both are subject to the audit fields defined in the Override & Administrative Action Audit Requirements.

  3. ### ***Reliability***

* The system shall target ≥95% uptime during the pilot deployment period within the academic semester.  
* All database write operations for submission state changes and slot reservations shall be executed within ACID-compliant transactions to ensure data integrity.  
* The publishing workflow shall be able to continue via manual recovery (UC-2.4 A8) in the event of sustained Facebook Graph API unavailability.  
* The system shall handle Facebook Graph API failures gracefully: automated publishing failures shall trigger up to three retry attempts with exponential backoff (5s, 25s, 125s) per GR-T5. If all retries fail, the submission transitions to `PUBLISH_FAILED` status and the Administrator receives in-app and email alerts (T-06). Manual resolution becomes available via the Approval Queue's Failed tab (UC-2.4 A8).  
* The system shall handle AI service unavailability (caption generation, image classification, embedding) gracefully without displaying errors to the user. All AI features degrade silently, and the submission workflow shall remain fully functional without AI assistance.  
* Email notification delivery failures shall be recorded as failed in the email\_delivery\_log for administrative review; each email is attempted once, with no automatic retry. In-app notifications shall function independently of email delivery and are triggered instantly via an event-driven listener rather than a polling queue.  
* Slot reservations shall be guaranteed atomic: two Contributors attempting to reserve the same slot simultaneously shall result in only one successful reservation, with the second receiving a clear "slot no longer available" message and a list of alternatives (UC-1.9 A4).  
* The Approaching Publish Time Priority Flag (GR-T1) shall ensure no submission's urgency is silently missed: submissions nearing their scheduled time without a review decision carry a priority badge in the Approval Queue (UC-2.4). If a submission's scheduled time passes without a decision, it transitions to MISSED\_REVIEW (GR-T9) and is listed in the Failed tab, where a new slot returns it to review (UC-2.4 A8).  
* The system shall implement database backup procedures to prevent data loss. Backup frequency shall be at minimum once per day during the deployment period (provided automatically by Supabase managed backups).  
* Background jobs shall record each run in scheduled\_job\_runs, be visible on System Health, and be re-runnable by an Administrator (UC-3.5). Only the latest run per job is exposed; a failed run is not restarted automatically and is retried on its next schedule. The 16 tracked jobs are:  
  * Publishing Scheduler (every minute — UC-3.2)  
  * Stale Submission Detector (every 5 minutes — GR-T9)  
  * Token Publishing Escalation (every 5 minutes — UC-3.2 A3)  
  * Validation Deadline Notification (every 5 minutes)  
  * Abandonment Detector (every 5 minutes — manual publishing, BR-PUB-06)  
  * Review Lock Cleanup (every minute)  
  * Social Engagement Sync (every 15 minutes)  
  * Embedding Reconciliation (every 30 seconds — GR-T7)  
  * Invitation Expiry (hourly — GR-T8)  
  * Stale Draft Slot Release (daily — GR-T2)  
  * Media Asset Retention Purge (daily — 30-day Trash lifecycle)  
  * Generated Watermark Purge (daily — 3-day derivative retention)  
  * Scheduled Job Run Retention (daily)  
  * Token Health Check (daily — GR-T3, GR-T4)  
  * Embedding Failure Digest (weekly — T-12)  
  * Empty Schedule Warning (weekly — T-07)

  Also scheduled but not tracked on System Health: Audit Log Retention (daily), Revoked Token Cleanup (hourly), and the media-processing worker (polls every second).

* The system shall automatically attempt cleanup of orphaned staged Facebook photos (photos uploaded via the two-step publishing method where the subsequent feed post call failed) via `DELETE /{photo_id}` before transitioning a submission to `PUBLISH_FAILED`. If cleanup fails, the photo IDs that could not be deleted shall be recorded on the publication attempt and listed for the Administrator in a consolidated alert, ensuring no silent accumulation of orphaned content on the DASIG Facebook Page (UC-3.2 A1). 

  4. ### ***Scalability*** {#scalability}

* The system shall support at least 50 concurrent users without degradation in primary workflow performance.

* The system shall support at least 12 active member institutions, with the design accommodating future expansion to 25 institutions without architectural changes.

* The database shall support at least 10,000 submissions and 50,000 media assets without query performance degradation. This is guaranteed by the following optimized indexes: 

  * submissions(institution\_id)

  * submissions(status)

  * submissions(scheduled\_at) — implemented as a **partial index** targeting only unresolved statuses (e.g., scheduled, publishing) to optimize scheduler memory.

  * media\_asset\_embeddings(embedding) — implemented via a pgvector **HNSW** index for highly scalable cosine distance searches.

  * users(institution\_id)

  * notifications(recipient\_id, created\_at DESC) — composite index for fast inbox hydration.

* To prevent memory degradation during concurrent AI usage, image payloads are dynamically resized in-memory to \< 5 MB prior to API transmission. Overall AI feature usage shall scale with the configured rate limits; cost is bounded by the per-user rate limits defined above.

  5. ### ***Maintainability and Auditability*** {#maintainability-and-auditability}

* All system actions involving state changes shall be auditable through the audit log table, viewable via Audit Log Review (UC-3.6).

* Operational health metrics (approval turnaround time, Edit & Approve rate, manual fallback resolution rate, publishing success rate, missed-review rate, Live Event Fast-Track volume) shall be exposed to Administrators on the System Health screen (UC-3.5), with on-time publication and related workflow metrics on the Analytics dashboard (UC-3.4).

* Guard rail thresholds (conflict buffer duration, per-institution quota, lead-time bounds, posting window, daily volume cap) and the enforcement switch shall be configurable by the Administrator without requiring code changes; trigger rule thresholds are fixed in code (Section 3.3), supporting iterative tuning based on operational experience. These thresholds are exposed in Settings → Page (UC-1.4). Each threshold displays its current value, a valid input range, and a plain-language description of its operational effect. Threshold changes record the updating Administrator and time on the settings row; writing them to the immutable audit log with previous and new values is required but not yet implemented (known gap). Changes take effect immediately on save and apply to all subsequent slot selections and guard rail evaluations network-wide.

* The system architecture (three-layer self-service / automation / exception model) is documented to support future maintainers in understanding the design philosophy and making consistent enhancement decisions.

  6. ### ***Data Retention*** {#data-retention}

* Submission records and media asset metadata shall be retained for the duration of the pilot deployment period plus six months.  
* In-app notification panel entries shall display the Top 50 most recent notifications for immediate access. All older notifications shall be accessible only via the paginated full-history view (UC-3.3).  
* Notification and email delivery logs (event type, target user ID, channel, message template ID, timestamp, delivery status) shall be retained indefinitely during the pilot deployment period, as no automated truncation is applied to these operational tables.  
* Audit log entries utilize a tiered retention policy: routine operational actions (sign-ins, uploads, background jobs) are retained for 730 days. Compliance-critical events (state changes, hard rule overrides, access events, guard rail threshold changes) are append-only and retained indefinitely to guarantee a permanent compliance trail.  
* Raw media files stored in Cloudflare R2 operate on a soft-delete lifecycle. Active media is retained indefinitely. When an asset is deleted it moves to the Trash and its AI vector embeddings are removed; after a 30-day grace period the MediaAssetRetentionPurgeJob permanently deletes the raw file from R2 and the asset record. An Administrator may restore an asset from the Trash, or permanently delete it earlier (UC-2.3 A5). Generated watermark derivatives are deleted after 3 days.

  7. ### ***Accessibility*** {#accessibility}

* The system's web interface shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA success criteria for all primary user-facing pages, including: the login page, content submission form, validation queue, master calendar, media library, and analytics dashboard.  
* All form fields shall include descriptive, programmatically associated labels.  
* All informational images shall include meaningful alternative text. Decorative images shall use empty alt attributes (`alt=""`).  
* Color shall not be used as the sole means of conveying information. Submission status badges shall include both a color indicator and a text label (e.g., "PENDING" text alongside the yellow badge).  
* All interactive elements (buttons, links, form inputs) shall be keyboard-navigable and shall display a visible focus indicator.  
* The calendar reschedule confirmation dialog shall enforce basic role limits prior to confirmation. Heavy guard rail evaluations (slot conflicts, quotas) are enforced upon submission of the dialog, with violations displayed as inline errors to the user. 

  8. ### ***Usability*** {#usability}

* The system shall achieve a minimum System Usability Scale (SUS) score of ≥70 (Proposal GO2; above the 68 "average" threshold per Bangor, Kortum, and Miller, 2009\) as measured through formal SUS evaluation during the pilot deployment window.  
* SUS evaluation shall be conducted with a minimum of 10 participants drawn from the pilot user population (Contributors and Administrators combined).  
* Participants shall complete evaluation tasks covering the primary workflows: content submission, content approval, failed-publication recovery, account provisioning, and master calendar access.  
* A SUS score below 70 shall trigger a mandatory usability review and targeted revision cycle before any full deployment proceeds.  
* SUS scores shall be recorded per role (Contributor, Administrator) in addition to the aggregate score, to identify role-specific usability issues.  
* Learnability (REQ-126): first-time users shall complete their role's core task without assistance in ≥95% of attempts, measured from the task-event log (Section 3.6.2) and confirmed by SUS ≥70 after the pilot.  
* Mobile operability (REQ-218): see Section 3.6.4.  
* MVP validation result (13–21 September 2026, 16 sessions): SUS 61.8 (66.1 excluding straight-lined responses) and 6 of 16 sessions completed without help — both below target; see Section 3.6.

  5. ## ***Tenant Isolation (Multi-Institution Data Separation)*** {#tenant-isolation-(multi-institution-data-separation)}

Because DASIGConnect is a multi-tenant system serving multiple independent institutions, the most critical security boundary in the system is the strict separation of data between institutions. A Contributor at CIT-U must never see a submission from Silliman; a Contributor at USC must never see media from CIT-U. This subsection defines how tenant isolation is enforced. 

1. ### ***Core Principle*** {#core-principle}

Every Contributor user is permanently associated with exactly one institution at the time of account creation, recorded as `users.institution_id`. Every submission, asset, and institution-scoped record carries an `institution_id` foreign key. The system enforces that users can only access records whose `institution_id` matches their own.

Administrators and Moderators are the only users with `institution_id = NULL`, signifying network-wide authority. They bypass tenant filters by design to perform exception-handling and governance functions.

2. ### ***Enforcement Mechanism (Defense in Depth)*** {#enforcement-mechanism-(defense-in-depth)}

Tenant isolation is enforced through four complementary layers, ensuring that no single point of failure can result in cross-institution data leakage: 

* **Layer 1 — JWT-Based Tenant Binding.** When a user authenticates, the JWT token issued contains their institution\_id as a verified claim, signed by the server using HS256 and a secret key (JWT\_SECRET), making it tamper-proof. On every authenticated request, the server verifies the token signature and reads the institution\_id claim, attaching a tenant filter to the request context before any controller logic executes. Moderators and Administrators receive a null filter (network-wide access); Contributors receive a filter restricted to their own institution.  
* **Layer 2 — Application Query Filters.** Every database query that accesses institution-scoped data (submissions, assets, notifications, audit logs) must apply the tenant filter from the request context. This is enforced through code review and a dedicated test suite that verifies every controller method respects the filter. Queries are written using parameterized statements to prevent SQL injection: `WHERE institution_id = $1`, with the value bound to the `institution_id` resolved from the authenticated user's security context.  
* **Layer 3 — PostgreSQL Row-Level Security.** As a database-level safeguard, Row-Level Security (RLS) policies are enabled on all institution-scoped tables. The policies enforce that even if a developer mistakenly omits the application-layer tenant filter, the database itself returns zero rows for cross-institution queries. The RLS policies reference application-set session variables (`app.current_institution_id`, `app.current_role`, and `app.current_user_id`) that are bound to the database transaction via `TenantScopeService` at the start of each request based on the authenticated user. (The user ID is specifically required so the database can expose pending, un-instituted staged media uploads back to their creator).   
* **Layer 4 — Server-Derived Institution Identity.** The system never trusts client-supplied `institution_id` values. When a Contributor creates a new submission, the `institution_id` of the new record is automatically set from the authenticated user's session identity, not from the request body. Even if a malicious client attempts to specify a different institution in the request payload, the server overrides it.

  3. ### ***Visibility by Role and Feature*** {#visibility-by-role-and-feature}

The following table summarizes how tenant isolation manifests at each user-facing feature:  
	

| Feature | Contributor | Moderator | Administrator |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Review Queue | No access | Network-wide | Network-wide |
| Master Calendar (timing) | Network-wide, read-only | Network-wide, editable (Subject to reschedule caps & time windows) | Network-wide, editable |
| Master Calendar (content detail) | Own institution only | Network-wide | Network-wide |
| Media Library | Own institution \+ shared DASIG Central Visayas library | Network-wide  | Network-wide (always on; no toggle) |
| Analytics Dashboard | Own institution only | Network-wide (no institution filter) | Network-wide with optional institution filter |
| Audit Logs | Not accessible | Not accessible | Network-wide |
| User Management | Not accessible | Not accessible | Network-wide |

Master Calendar (content detail): Own institution only *(plus the "DASIG Central Visayas" network-wide default institution, visible in full to all Contributors)*.

The Master Calendar's timing layer is intentionally network-wide for read access, even for Contributors. This deliberate exception supports the self-service scheduling model: Contributors must see what slots are taken across all institutions to choose realistic times. However, full content (caption, media, description) of posts from other institutions is never returned in API responses to non-Administrator users — only timing and institution badge.

4. ### ***Cross-Institution Access Attempts*** {#cross-institution-access-attempts}

When a Contributor attempts to access a resource belonging to another institution (via URL guessing or manipulated API requests), the system intercepts the request at the service layer. A submission belonging to another institution returns HTTP 403 Forbidden. A media asset outside the user's visible institutions returns HTTP 404 Not Found, so its existence is not revealed (UC-2.2 A2). Database RLS backs up both. A request to an endpoint the user's role may not use returns 403 Forbidden.

5. ### ***Audit Logging of Administrator Cross-Institution Actions*** {#audit-logging-of-administrator-cross-institution-actions}

Any Administrator action that changes data for a specific institution — resolving a failed publication on an institution's behalf (UC-2.4 A8), reassigning a user, moving assets between institutions, or overriding a guard rail — is recorded in the audit log with the affected institution's ID and, where applicable, the reason for the cross-institution action. Read-only views, including institution-filtered analytics and Network View browsing in the Media Library (BR-MED-01), are not audited; routine non-decision events were removed from the audit log on 21 September 2026\.

6. ### ***Tenant Isolation Testing*** {#tenant-isolation-testing}

Tenant isolation is verified through automated unit and controller-slice tests (for example TenantScopeServiceTest, InstitutionControllerAuthTest, MediaAssetServiceTest, AccessDeniedAuditRecorderTest). A full cross-institution test of every API endpoint against a live database has not been performed and is planned for the pilot (STD v2.1). The tests are intended to verify that:

* All query results are correctly filtered by institution.  
* Direct-access attempts by ID are refused (404 for media assets; 403 for submissions).  
* All direct-access attempts by ID return 404\.  
* All write attempts to other-institution resources are rejected.  
* Administrator users correctly bypass filters when their role is verified.  
* Audit log entries are written for cross-institution Administrator actions that change data.

These tests run in the backend CI workflow on pushes to main and on pull requests into main, and must pass before merging to the main branch.

6. ## ***Validation-Driven Requirement Changes*** {#validation-driven-requirement-changes}

These requirements come from the MVP Validation Findings & Refactoring Priorities (12 Oct 2026). Each is **Approved — not implemented** in release v3.0.2 unless stated otherwise. Acceptance tests are in STD v2.1 (Case-29, Case-30) and traceability in RTM v2.1 Section 4\.

### ***3.6.1. Submission Gate Separate from Quality Tips — REQ-124 (RP-01, VF-01; High)*** {#3.6.1.-submission-gate-separate-from-quality-tips-—-req-124-(rp-01,-vf-01;-high)}

* **Finding:** a Contributor with a complete, valid post saw "90 %" and believed submission was blocked; it was the only task failure in the study (GO1, SO 1.7, RQ2).  
* **Requirement:** UC-1.5 and UC-1.9 "readiness" is redefined as the required-check gate only. The composer shall show a binary status ("Required: 7 of 7 — Ready to submit"), name the next missing item with a jump link while incomplete, and make Submit the primary always-visible action when the gate passes. Recommended items shall appear separately as optional tips ("Tips: 3 of 5 applied") with no percentage.  
* **Acceptance:** STD Case-30a; re-validation first-attempt completion ≥ 95 %; share of gate-passed drafts not submitted within 24 hours.  
* **Status:** **Implemented (`refactor/p1-submission-gate`)** — binary 7-of-7 Required Submission Gate (`Required: 7 of 7 ✓ — Ready to submit`) separated from 5 optional Post Quality Tips (`Tips: X of 5 applied`), with no blended percentage and a primary always-visible **Submit for Approval** action once the gate passes.

### ***3.6.2. Next Action, Plain-Language Status, and Task Instrumentation — REQ-125, REQ-126 (RP-02, VF-02; High)*** {#3.6.2.-next-action,-plain-language-status,-and-task-instrumentation-—-req-125,-req-126-(rp-02,-vf-02;-high)}

* **Finding:** 15 of 16 participants were satisfied, but only 6 of 16 sessions were completed without help; SUS 61.8 (GO2, SO 1.3).  
* **REQ-125:** each role's home screen shall lead with the single most important pending action (Contributor: "Finish your draft — 1 required item left"; Moderator: "3 submissions awaiting review — Review next"; Administrator: "1 failed publication needs action"). Every submission status shall state what it means and who acts next, using the same wording in the UI and notifications (e.g., "Needs revision — the Moderator asked for changes. Edit and resubmit."). The system shall record the start and finish of each role's core task to compute first-attempt completion and Time-on-Task.  
* **REQ-126 (NFR — learnability):** see Section 3.4.8.  
* **Acceptance:** STD Case-30b; re-validation and pilot logs.  
* **Status:** **Implemented (`refactor/p2-first-time-independence`)** — role-based Next Action card (`GET /api/v1/me/next-action` + `DashboardScreen`), shared plain-language `statusCopy` across UI and `NotificationEventListener`, and V123 `task_events` / `task_completion_logs` instrumentation (`POST /api/v1/task-events`, `GET /api/v1/telemetry/tasks/summary`).

### ***3.6.3. AI Caption on Upload, Media First, Log-Based Measurement — REQ-320, REQ-321 (RP-03, VF-03; High)*** {#3.6.3.-ai-caption-on-upload,-media-first,-log-based-measurement-—-req-320,-req-321-(rp-03,-vf-03;-high)}

* **Finding:** captions were generated only on request; 6 of 16 participants met any AI feature; 4 of 5 who saw a caption accepted it (GO3(c)(d), SO 1.6, RQ5).  
* **REQ-320:** once a draft has ≥ 1 image and an event title, the system shall generate a caption suggestion in the background and offer it inline as "AI draft ready — Use / Edit / Dismiss", never inserting it automatically. For each suggestion the system shall log generated, used, used-after-edit, or dismissed, a one-click 1–5 quality rating at decision time, and the time from opening Post Details to saving a caption. Existing rate limits apply; failure falls back to manual entry without blocking.  
* **REQ-321:** suggested media shall be the default media-picker view once there is enough event context; GO3(c) and GO3(d) shall be computed from these logs over ≥ 20 pilot submissions (coverage \= suggestions ÷ submissions with images; acceptance \= used \+ used-after-edit ÷ generated; quality \= mean rating).  
* **Acceptance:** STD Case-30c (**PASS**).  
* **Status:** **Implemented (`refactor/p3-ai-caption-on-upload`).** Background AI caption generation on first image upload + event title (`useAiCaptionAssist`), inline `"AI draft ready — Use / Edit / Dismiss"` banner with 1–5 quality rating and drafting duration telemetry (`AiCaptionSuggestion`, `CaptionController`, `V123__ai_caption_suggestions_telemetry.sql`), and media-first default tab (`MediaAssetsPicker`) are implemented and verified.

### ***3.6.4. Mobile Operability of Role-Critical Actions — REQ-218 (RP-04, VF-04; Medium)*** {#3.6.4.-mobile-operability-of-role-critical-actions-—-req-218-(rp-04,-vf-04;-medium)}

* **Finding:** 8 of 16 sessions were on phones or tablets; a Moderator could not find the review button; Moderator SUS 58.1 (GO2(a)(b), SO 2.4, SO 3.3, SO 1.9, RQ6).  
* **Requirement (NFR):** at 360 px width each role-critical action — submit, approve, request revision, reject, reschedule, resolve a failed publication, accept an invitation — shall be reachable on its screen without horizontal scrolling, through a persistent primary-action bar. Messenger and email alerts shall open the exact submission in review mode.  
* **Acceptance:** STD Case-29 on 360 × 800 and 768 × 1024 viewports, automated in Playwright.  
* **Status:** Implemented (refactor/p4-mobile-operability) and verified by STD Case-29 (Playwright mobile-operability.spec.ts across 360×800 and 768×1024 viewports and JUnit NotificationEventListenerTest).

### ***3.6.5. Bulk Invitations with Preview and Batch Audit — REQ-127 (RP-05, VF-05; Low–Medium)*** {#3.6.5.-bulk-invitations-with-preview-and-batch-audit-—-req-127-(rp-05,-vf-05;-low–medium)}

* **Finding:** form-by-form invitations (≤ 15 emails, one role and institution per form, errors only after sending) will not scale to network provisioning (SO 1.3, SO 1.10, GO1).  
* **Requirement:** Administrators and Moderators shall upload or paste rows of `email, role, institution`. Before sending, every row is validated and shown with its status (duplicate in batch, invalid email, unknown or inactive institution, active account exists, deactivated account — use Reactivation, pending invite to be superseded, would exceed the Administrator cap). Only valid rows are sent, in one confirmed action, through a server batch endpoint that repeats the validation and returns per-row results. One batch-summary audit record links the per-invitation records. Moderators may batch-invite Contributors only. Open self-registration is rejected for this version (conflicts with SO 1.4) and recorded as a possible future feature behind an approval queue.  
* **Acceptance:** STD Case-30d; Administrator time per provisioned user (10–20 users, ≥ 2 roles and institutions).  
* **Status:** Not implemented.

### ***3.6.6. Status Wording for Notifications and Submissions*** {#3.6.6.-status-wording-for-notifications-and-submissions}

Covered by REQ-125: notification messages and status labels shall use one shared plain-language copy table so the same sentence appears in the UI, email, and Messenger.
